method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Optometry Australia '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration' (approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022)). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: No licence or copyright statement in the PDF or on the Optometry Australia site; treated as all rights reserved (read at the PDF itself (no statement found) and https://www.optometry.org.au/). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **AMD is the leading cause of irreversible vision loss in Australians over 50.**
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Smoking is the biggest risk you can change:** it at least doubles AMD risk, so advise every tobacco user to stop.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Five-year progression risk rises steeply with stage:** about 3.1% for early AMD (medium drusen only), but around 47.3% once both eyes have large drusen and pigment change.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Differentials in which neovascularisation forms without drusen:** polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy, ocular histoplasmosis, pathological myopia, choroidal rupture, angioid streaks and idiopathic CNV. Consider diabetic macular oedema when the macula shows blood, lipid, exudate or fluid.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Warn about Charles Bonnet syndrome:** people with late AMD and poor sight in both eyes can get visual hallucinations, which are distressing and often need counselling.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected or definite new choroidal neovascular membrane: send to an ophthalmologist as an urgent referral, to be seen within one week.** Where ophthalmology is hard to reach, get a telehealth opinion by e-referral in the same week.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Urgent-referral triggers:** vision loss, distortion reported unprompted, or a new missing or blurred patch in central vision within the last 3 months; or signs of new CNV, fluid under or within the retina at the macula, or bleeding there that nothing else explains.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Speed matters:** vision at presentation is among the strongest predictors of long-term acuity, so the sooner treatment starts, the better the chance of keeping or gaining vision.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **OCT is among the most useful tests:** it shows active neovascular disease such as retinal fluid. Get an OCT whenever new symptoms appear or neovascular AMD is suspected, and refer if needed.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Intravitreal anti-VEGF injection is the mainstay of treatment.** In Australia the main agents are ranibizumab and aflibercept, with bevacizumab used off-label. Their efficacy is similar, so availability, injection frequency and cost usually decide the choice.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start with injections at fixed monthly intervals until the lesion shows no activity** (for example, no fluid on OCT).
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat and extend:** each time there is no sign of active CNV (no OCT fluid, no loss of 5 letters, no new haemorrhage), the gap to the next injection grows by 2 weeks. Visual results match monthly dosing.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **As-needed (PRN), monthly-or-bimonthly and observe-and-plan schedules are options,** but they generally do worse than treat and extend or monthly injections.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Thermal laser and photodynamic therapy are now rare,** kept mostly for polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy with a well-defined lesion away from the fovea.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The guide notes no approved treatment for geographic atrophy;** review it every six to twelve months, with the interval set by vision, driving status and risk of progression, and offer low-vision care. It can convert to neovascular AMD, so teach Amsler-grid use.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **For intermediate AMD, the AREDS2 formula may help:** vitamin C 500 mg, vitamin E 400 IU, zinc 80 mg (as zinc oxide), copper 2 mg (as cupric oxide), lutein 10 mg and zeaxanthin 2 mg. ⚠️ That zinc dose is above the Australian and New Zealand upper intake limit, so discuss it with the GP.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Supplements are not advised** for early AMD, for normal age-related changes only, when both eyes already have late AMD, or for at-risk people without any AMD signs.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Teach home Amsler-grid monitoring at every visit,** and tell the patient to come in at once for distortion, central blur or vision loss.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review without new symptoms:** early AMD at least every 12 months; intermediate AMD every 6 to 12 months (per the guide's review table).
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Early or intermediate AMD does not need an ophthalmologist** unless there is a strong family history (possible inherited dystrophy), atypical findings including onset before age 50, or the patient wants to join a trial.
claims.locator: Optometry Australia, '2019 Clinical Practice Guide for the diagnosis, treatment and management of age-related macular degeneration', approved 8 February 2019 (due for revision 2022), https://www.optometry.org.au/wp-content/uploads/Professional_support/Practice_notes/AMD-Clinical-Practice-Guide-2019_final_designed_v5.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-23
